## Design summary
- Currency identity is issuer + immutable definition; display names are labels. Each definition selects graph-native or ledger-anchored semantics.
- Graph-native balances are offline folds where double-spends are detectable, not preventable; ledger-anchored balances are online TigerBeetle truth with graph authorization/audit.
- Real-service grants use pending ledger holds, stay unspendable through the refund window, and attach post-activation shortfall to the grantee; payment receipts are non-monetary.
- Anchored conversions use a signed per-direction `currency.rate_authorisation`, 60-second event-pinned quote, linked atomic batch, write-ahead intent, and same-ID recovery; posted value is compensated, never edited.
- The note adopts the newest #2290/#2063/#2804 recommendations where they refine merged #2741, and defines rotation, snapshots, fold/index placement, OSS boundary, invariants, and acceptance tests.
- Docs-only: no implementation code changed; Drew’s policy choices are recorded with recommended defaults and do not block the contract phases.

**Design note:** [doc/2026-11-01_design_id2043.md](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/design/id-2043/doc/2026-11-01_design_id2043.md)  
**PR:** https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3886

**Phased plan:** (1) reconcile wire contracts/vectors (#2251/#3800); (2) graph-native core (#2803); (3) registry/gateway (#2062 F1–F3); (4) anchored transfers/snapshots (#2062 F4–F5/#2298); (5) rate authorization/conversion executor (#3801–#3802/#2289); (6) grants/receipts (#2042/#2296); (7) client UX and OSS release (#2803). Each is a separate PR; dependencies and gates are in the note.

**Questions for Drew (recommendations in bold):**
1. Public name: choose `id bucks`, `d3v`, `dt`, `2d`, `d2d`, or leave unset; **recommend defer branding** and show neutral “units” until chosen.
2. Supply: finite cap or `open`; **recommend a finite definition-time cap for every v1 issuer** to bound key-compromise damage.
3. Recovery: cold recovery-key commitment mandatory for anchored currencies or optional everywhere; **recommend mandatory for anchored, optional for graph-native**.
4. Emergency platform revoke: issuer-only graph revocation + logged local gateway suspension, or a second platform-signed graph revoke; **recommend issuer-only graph authority**.
5. Grant terms: #2296 options are 14 days, 48 hours, early vest on evidence, or no hold; **recommend 14 days for Steam-direct, publisher terms per retail source, and pending units never spendable**. For #2042’s other open parameters, recommend source-specific chargeback horizons, no debt expiry, signed/public write-off, first-party `for-cause` revocation, case-by-case good-faith relief, and no grant expiry unless declared; `posting_grace` stays an explicit operator setting.
6. Open-source boundary: open graph/client code only or all correctness-critical service/gateway/reconciliation code; **recommend open-source all correctness-critical code**, with production secrets, customer data, and deployment-specific config kept private.

Snapshot signer/cadence, client vs shared fold, and receipt/reversal semantics have explicit defaults in the note; no additional Drew ruling is requested on those.

# Drew's policy rulings on #2043 — recorded 2026-11-08

Drew ruled on the six policy questions from the merged design (PR #3886) in the main chat on 2026-11-08 (questions 1–5 at 07:14 CST, question 6 at 07:15 CST). His words, verbatim:

> 1 yes, units and pending units and revoked units 3 currencies 2 finite except transfers from the account for supplying currency, named like tiger beetle would be. 3 yes 4 yes 5 yes except allow trading pending units if both parties accept/sign. transfer cancel option that originator can trade their pending units 1:1 for revoked units not after (14 days from Init) which also attaches the notBefore trade from pending units to units. only trade able as a chained item from initial grant by us. any pending units without a provided option contract will be denied by us to trade in, our clients will require it as an input for any pending unit trade. at 28 days notAfter signature is enabled, we automatically sign and put the transfer at 14 days and each users contracted other users can redeem against that users account using their signed chained contract, they can oresubmit signs counterdigned contracts to us and we will run as soon as all the chains up to them are done. maybe our clients require all such contracts are submitted to us by pending unit owner and then other party ckuntersigns only transactions escrowed to us with all chains up to original also escrowed so they can know they'll either get units or rejected units as we process entire batch atomically?

Question 6, verbatim (07:15 CST):

> yes open

## Mapped outcomes

### CONFIRMED (recommendation accepted as stated)

- Q3 — Recovery key: mandatory for ledger-anchored, optional for graph-native. ("3 yes")
- Q4 — Emergency revocation: issuer-only, gateway suspension local and logged. ("4 yes")
- Q6 — Open-source boundary: open all correctness-critical code. ("yes open")

### CONFIRMED WITH MODIFICATIONS

- Q1 — Public name: "units" confirmed as the neutral label (branding deferred, as recommended). MODIFICATION: Drew names three currencies — **units**, **pending units**, and **revoked units**.
- Q2 — Supply: finite cap confirmed. MODIFICATION: finite *except transfers from the account for supplying currency*.
- Q5 — Grant terms (#2296): base terms accepted. MODIFICATION: pending units may be **traded** under a chained option-contract mechanism — full ruling recorded on #2296.

### UNRESOLVED (recorded verbatim, no interpretation adopted)

- Q2: "named like tiger beetle would be" — what this names, and how the supply-account exception interacts with the finite cap, is not settled by the text.
- Q5: several phrases in the trading mechanism are unclear as written; they are listed on #2296 and need Drew's confirmation before they are treated as design.

## Where this extends or conflicts with the merged design (PR #3886, doc/2026-11-01_design_id2043.md)

- **Three currencies:** the design has no "revoked units" currency. In the design, "pending" is a hold state on the same ledger-anchored currency (a pending TigerBeetle hold, unspendable until the refund window closes), and revocation is an event/policy (issuer revocation, gateway suspension, per-definition revocation policy) — not a currency. Drew's units / pending units / revoked units as three currencies EXTENDS the design and needs a design follow-up: three distinct currency definitions, or balance classes/states of one currency?
- **Supply exception:** the design requires a finite cap for every v1 currency (Invariant 2; §8 Q2 recommendation) with no exception for a supply account. Drew's exception for "transfers from the account for supplying currency" is new. Whether transfers out of that account count against the cap is UNRESOLVED.
- **Pending trading:** the design says pending units are never spendable, and #2296's Decision 2 recommendation is "not spendable, at all." Neither the design nor #2296 contains any pending-trading notion. Drew's ruling keeps pending unspendable as spending but adds tradability between parties who both accept/sign, under chained option contracts — a new mechanism that modifies #2296 Decision 2 as written. Detail on #2296.

All six questions are now answered. The UNRESOLVED points above are interpretation questions on Drew's modifications, not unanswered questions.

The rulings themselves stay as recorded above; the PR designs how the modifications fit and changes nothing in the settled base design.
It covers: the three-currency model (units / pending units / revoked units, both structural readings with ledger implications), the supply-account cap exception (definition, mint/burn accounting, replacement wording for Invariant 2), and the full pending-unit trading mechanism for #2296, including the atomic batch escrow variant designed as an option (your open proposal, not treated as a ruling).
Recommendation headlines: three currencies are best implemented as three balance classes on one ledger, presented and ruled as three currencies (three full definitions are also designed, if that's what you intend); supply-account transfers should count against the cap, net of returns, or the cap is unenforceable; the sequential chained-contract design is recommended for v1 over atomic escrow.
The unresolved phrases are collected in §4 of the doc (U1–U7), quoted verbatim with the exact clarification each needs — including "named like tiger beetle would be," which is interpreted nowhere.

body:
**Follow-on ruling recorded — §1 rewritten as double entry.**

Drew ruled **"double entry"** on 2026-11-08 09:13 CST, replying to the PR #7722 summary whose §1 had recommended "three balance classes on one ledger."

§1 of the extension doc in [PR #7722](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7722) is rewritten accordingly (new commit `5ce3af3d22`, same branch): one ledger, the three currencies (units / pending units / revoked units) as account classes, a chart of accounts, a journal-entry table for every event type (issuance, grant, vest, cancel, revocation, trade, payment, burn, escrow), invariants DE-1–DE-6 in double-entry terms, and a TigerBeetle mapping. This supersedes the two-readings fork and the balance-classes recommendation.

**U7 is answered by this ruling and removed** from the unresolved list (disposition noted in §4 of the doc): "double entry" fixes the structure at the journal level, so the definitions-vs-classes fork no longer needs a separate answer for v1.

## Terminology + future extensions — Drew's 2026-11-08 clarifications recorded, doc updated in PR #7722

Drew, 2026-11-08 09:26 CST, verbatim:

> <and exact use isn't currency necessarily they are merely tokens, currency is just the tigerbeetle term and often used for representation grants and capabilities offered fora server or world. they hold no value, by definition, same as gold in wow or rp in lol 9r mayberoblox

And Drew, 2026-11-08 09:27 CST, approving the future-extensions section on a condition:

> yes as long as we didn't write this in a way that isn't conducive to future changes while maintaining and transitioning system and features — it's fine to defer most things we haven't covered, so long as it's at least a little thought through architecturally.

Both are now recorded in the design extension in PR #7722 (new commit `3017caba8d`, on top of the double-entry rewrite):

- **One-line mapping: "currency" is TigerBeetle's term; our term is token.** New doc §0 ("What a token is"): a token is a representation of grants and capabilities offered for a server or a world; it holds **no value by definition** — not money, not stored value, not redeemable (Drew's analogies: gold in World of Warcraft, RP in League of Legends, Robux in Roblox). TigerBeetle `ledger` = one token system (one grant programme); where the base design or TigerBeetle says "currency," read "token." The base design doc is not rewritten — §0 states the reading for it.
- **Terminology pass** over the extension doc's own prose: the three classes are token classes (Units / Pending / Revoked keep their account-class names); issuance, supply, trades, and conversions are worded in token terms. Identifiers are unchanged: the `currency.*` graph event types and the currency-service component name stay (renaming identifiers is a migration, not a terminology pass). Quoted rulings and the §4 UNRESOLVED items are untouched.
- **Consequences, as noted in §0 and in place:** §1 / DE invariants — unchanged (conservation is integrity of grant accounting, not value). §2 — issuance is entitlement issuance; the cap is a scarcity/integrity control on grants, not monetary policy. §3 — trades transfer entitlements; "consideration" never prices the token (units of the same token in-system, or off-ledger recorded by hash, unpriced and unadjudicated).
- **New doc §6, "Future extensions — deferred, with seams":** the six gaps — anchored provisioning for user-created token systems; a backend dimension on the binding; cross-backend atomicity; ledger-type migration mechanics; a per-token policy surface (the 14/14/28-day windows becoming definition fields); U6 ("rejected units") blocking escrow Variant E — each with what is deferred and the seam v1 leaves. Drew's condition is stated in §6 as a binding architectural rule for v1, and the two places the current text hard-wires something are named there as known narrowings with transition paths: §1's one-TigerBeetle-ledger-per-programme assumption, and the §3 windows as global constants.

Transcription readings in the 09:26 text, Drew's to correct if wrong: "9r" read as "or"; "mayberoblox" read as Roblox (its unit: Robux); "rp in lol" read as League of Legends' RP.

🤖 **Agent note** · unblocked — Drew's answer found (2026-11-11 audit follow-up, code#8097)

- **Task:** queue task 8586 (was blocked, reason class `escalated-to-user`)
- **Gate was:** Six explicit currency policy questions in merged design PR #3886: public name, supply cap, anchored recovery-key mandate, emergency platform-revoke authority, grant/hold terms, open-source boundary.
- **Drew's answer:** All six ruled by Drew 2026-11-08 (ledger item `policy-rulings-2043-six`; ruling recorded on this issue, comment 6721988851): (1) ship neutral label 'units' — three currencies named: units, pending units, revoked units; (2) finite cap, except transfers from the supply account; (3) recovery key mandatory for ledger-anchored, optional for graph-native; (4) issuer-only revocation, gateway suspension local/logged; (5) grant terms per #2296 ruling; (6) open all correctness-critical code. The modifications extend the merged design and need design follow-ups — fleet work, not a Drew gate.
- **Action:** task 8586 unblocked to `queued`; verified by read-back of the task row. Stale `user/escalated` / `queue/blocked` / `status/blocked` labels removed here; `queue/queued` added.

The six policy questions it left open were all ruled by Drew on 2026-11-08 (comment 6721988851) and the gate on this task was lifted today on that basis — no re-escalation; a recorded decision is never re-asked.
- **What remains (the triage routing):**
  1. The merged design doc still frames the six ruled questions as OPEN with recommendations (spot-checked on main: the token-name question at line ~141). Folding the rulings in is filed as issue #8576 with fix packet enqueued as task 14902.
  2. PR #7722 (extension doc carrying Drew's 2026-11-08 terminology clarifications + future extensions) is still OPEN at head 3017caba8d, unlabelled since 2026-11-08. Shepherd packet enqueued as task 14903.
- **Acceptance for the fix:** task 14902 lands the rulings in the design doc; task 14903 merges PR #7722. This issue stays open until both land.
